data.name: Clarette
data.gender_notes: Clarette is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Latin clarus, meaning clear, bright, and light. The name has been borne by several saints, including Saint Claire of Assisi and Saint Claire of Montefalco. The name Clarette carries the meaning “Clear, bright, light” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Clarette usually hope their child will grow to embody clear, bright, light and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Clarette belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Clear, bright, light.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Clarette total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

data.cultural_impact: The name Clararette can be considered a rare and unique name, reflecting its heritage from the Latin language. It evokes images of clarity, brightness, and grace, which have been cherished and celebrated in various cultures throughout history. For example, in the Middle Ages, the name Claire was a popular choice for noblewomen due to its association with light, purity, and elegance.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Clararette carries deeper meaning and symbolic importance. It is a reminder of the inner light and clarity that we all possess as human beings, and the importance of cultivating this light within ourselves through spiritual practices such as meditation, prayer, and self-reflection. The name also echoes the biblical reference to Christ as the "light of the world," and encourages us to reflect His light in our own lives and in our interactions with others. Ultimately, Clararette is a name that inspires us to strive for purity, clarity, and inner peace in our relationship with God and with ourselves.
